neutral_facts.value: The accused, an army officer, was involved in an altercation during a farewell party. The deceased attempted to intervene and was abused by the accused. After the party, the deceased was found in a pool of blood in his room. The accused was present in the room and was found lying on his bed. The deceased was taken to the hospital and declared dead. The accused surrendered at the police station and confessed to stabbing the deceased with a knife. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including witness testimonies and a medical report indicating the stab wound caused the death. The accused was alone in the room, and his absence from the 'fall in parade' and presence at the police station were considered against him. The trial court convicted him under Section 304 Part II of the IPC, and the conviction was upheld by the Armed Forces Tribunal and the Supreme Court.

quotes.text: After receiving the information from the J.C.O., the Commanding Officer, Col. Rajiv Chib, PW27, along with Lt. Col. Atul Kumar Bhat, PW15, reached the police station Sabina about 1.50 a.m. and enquired from the accused about the details to which he confessed that he had stabbed the deceased.

The present appeal, by special leave, is directed against the judgment of affirmation of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Armed Forces Tribunal, principal Bench, New Delhi (for short 'the tribunal') in T.A. 617 of 2009 whereby the tribunal has confirmed the conviction under Section 304 Part-II, l.P.C. and the sentence of seven years of rigorous imprisonment imposed by the General Court Martial held at Sabina in the State of Madhya Pradesh vide order dated 24.2.2007 and further has maintained the order dated 18.3.2008 passed by the Chief of Army Staff under Section 164(2) of the Army Act, 1950 (for brevity 'the Act').

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant was present in the room, had indulged in an altercation, was in a drunken state, and was alone in the room. The chain of circumstances was complete, and the appellant's presence at the police station and absence at the 'fall in parade' were against him. The confessional statement made by the appellant was voluntary and supported by the testimony of witnesses.

quotes.text: The said established facts which are founded on proper appreciation of the evidence by the forums below make clear that the chain of circumstances was complete. What has weighed with the forums below was that the appellant was present in the room and had escaped. The circumstances that really weighed against the appellant were that he had indulged in an altercation in the party; that he was in a drunken state and he was alone present in the room; and that he had escaped by the rear door.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the evidence contained discrepancies, the presence of other persons in the room was possible, and the non-recovery of the knife undermined the prosecution case. They also contended that the tribunal failed to analyze the discrepancies and relied on hearsay evidence, making the judgment perverse.

quotes.text: The presence of the accused at the time of incident as per the evidence available on record is doubtful and, therefore, the conclusion that has been arrived at deserves to be dislodged on the bedrock that it does not meet the criteria of proof as per the principles laid down by this Court in relation to acceptance of the circumstantial evidence.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is sought to be established must be conclusive in nature. The court emphasized that the chain of circumstances must be consistent only with the hypothesis of the appellant's guilt.

quotes.text: The circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is sought to be established must be conclusive in nature.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence of seven years of rigorous imprisonment was imposed because the accused should be aware of the consequences of his actions, and although he did not intend to kill, the injury caused was likely to result in death. The court found him guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II of the IPC.

quotes.text: Even though the accused had no intention to kill the deceased, the accused should be knowing the consequences of his action. The accused should be conscious, that by stabbing at chest, which is a vital part of a human body, the injured person is likely to die, due to the effect of such injury.

judicial_aggravating_factors.value: The appellant had indulged in an altercation in the party, was in a drunken state, was alone present in the room, and had escaped by the rear door. His presence at the police station and absence at the 'fall in parade' were aggravating factors.
